answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens and undergo randomized game-theoretic audits using topological cut verifications. Verifiers track the flow pulse across interaction graphs; if clustered nodes wander into low-expansion cuts mimicking real activity, multi-agent audits slash their bonded stake. Because verifying sparse cuts imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with O(n²), planting fake identities resembling a yarrow stalk becomes mathematically unprofitable.
